chunks: And al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd also narrated, from Faḍālah, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the woman in nifās: how long does she refrain? He said: “Indeed, Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays was instructed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to perform ghusl at eighteen, and there is no harm in her taking an extra precaution of a day or two.”

His statement عليه السلام, “Indeed, Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays was instructed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to perform ghusl at eighteen,” does not indicate that the days of nifās are eighteen. It only indicates that he instructed her, after eighteen, to perform ghusl. It would only have constituted proof if he had said, “The days of nifās are eighteen days,” and this is not in the report. Everything narrated that is similar to what we have narrated is addressed in the same manner.

We have several approaches in speaking about these reports. One of them is that these reports are solitary reports, differing in wording and contradictory in meaning. It is not possible to act upon all of them due to their contradiction, nor upon some of them, because some are not more deserving of being acted upon than others.

The second is that it is possible these reports were issued in the mode of taqiyyah, because everyone who opposes us holds that the days of nifās are more than what we say. For this reason, the wordings of the hadiths differed, just as the general body differed in their schools, as though they gave fatwa to each group among them according to what they knew of their views and schools.

The third is that it is possible the questioner asked them about a woman upon whom these days had passed and she had not performed ghusl, so they instructed her after that to perform ghusl and to act as the mustaḥāḍah acts. This does not indicate that what the woman had done during those days was correct. And that which clarifies what we have said...

key_terms.أَخْبَارُ آحَادٍ: solitary reports that do not reach mass transmission
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity in adverse circumstances
key_terms.النُّفَسَاءِ: a woman in the state of postnatal bleeding
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرَ: to take an added precaution by waiting extra time
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلَ: to perform ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.لِثَمَانِيَ عَشْرَةَ: at eighteen, referring here to the reported point for ghusl

ai.seo_question: Does the hadith about Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays prove that nifās lasts eighteen days?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling of nifās and discusses how a narration about Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays should be understood. The accompanying analysis argues that the report does not itself prove eighteen days as the fixed duration of nifās, and it outlines methodological reasons for caution in using such reports, including contradiction among narrations and the possibility of taqiyyah.
